central_unknown: Ferrari brought major upgrades and topped both FP1 and FP2, but historically they have flattered on Fridays and faded on race day. The key question is whether Ferrari's upgrade gains hold through qualifying and the race, and whether McLaren's big upgrade package (which Norris says may take time to dial in) closes the gap.

budget_tiers.fills: Hulkenberg, Bortoleto (differential gamble from back of grid)

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Charles Leclerc
captains.reason: ML projects 29.8 exp pts (proj 37.7), ppm 1.33, value 1.24, MEDIUM risk, predicted P1→P1. Topped both FP1 and FP2 at COTA. Ferrari brought 4 upgrades and looked genuinely fast. FanAmp considers him a lock. ML ranks him #1 captain by expected points. DNF risk 0.14 is the main concern, but upside (90% CI up to 51 pts) is enormous.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: ML projects 27.8 exp pts (proj 30.4), ppm 1.81, MEDIUM risk, predicted P4→P2. Was top 3 in both practice sessions. FanAmp had him as the default 2x before Friday but now rates Leclerc slightly higher. Concern: Hadjar said car looked 'horrendous' which could drag Red Bull constructor down. Still a strong captain if you prefer consistency at COTA.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: ML projects 24.0 exp pts (proj 30.1), ppm 1.11, LOW risk (only 4% DNF), predicted P3→P3, 90% CI [-2.8, 42.0]. Finished P2 in FP2. FanAmp considers him one of three must-have drivers alongside Leclerc and Verstappen. Lower ceiling than Leclerc but safest floor of the top 3 options.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Six consecutive price rises of 0.6M. 81% chance of another price increase per F1 Fantasy Tools. FP1 power unit complaints resolved after setup change in FP2. Budget cornerstone — virtually a must-have.

buy.name: Oliver Bearman
buy.note: 82% chance of price rise per F1 Fantasy Tools. Needs only -7 to -2 pts for price increase. Great budget filler alongside Hulkenberg.

buy.name: Liam Lawson
buy.note: ML projects 14.0 exp pts. F1FantasyPolePosition favors Lawson over Lindblad long-term due to upcoming 3-race average benefit from Singapore's big score. 82% chance of max price rise. Saves 0.1M vs Lindblad.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: ML projects 14.6 exp pts (proj 17.2), LOW risk (4% DNF), predicted P12→P10. Taking 5-place grid penalty — extra overtake opportunities. FanAmp rates him equal to Lawson with a slight edge on overtake potential.

consider.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
consider.note: ML projects 16.5 exp pts (proj 18.7), value 2.36 (highest on the grid), LOW risk, predicted P13→P13. Taking 20-place grid penalty — starts at the back behind Cadillac, Williams, Aston Martin. FanAmp says possible 15-20 pt day but will almost certainly lose 0.6M in price. High-risk/high-reward differential for teams with 140M+ budget.

consider.name: Esteban Ocon
consider.note: Scored 12 points in two consecutive races. 60% chance of price rise. Underrated per F1FantasyPolePosition. Alternative to Lawson/Lindblad at same price point.

consider.name: Fernando Alonso
consider.note: One-week budget saver option at 5.4M. 60% price rise chance. F1FantasyPolePosition sees him as a differential but COTA is power-dependent which doesn't suit Aston Martin.

avoid: Alex Albon — didn't complete a representative flying lap in either session due to track limits; Williams struggling badly at COTA
Franco Colapinto — 10-place grid penalty, DNF'd sprint and race at Singapore, needs 39 pts just to avoid price drop
Lance Stroll — Aston Martin looked poor in practice
Williams constructor — worst performer on Friday

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: If you need to restructure for the final triple-header (US/Mexico/São Paulo), a Wildcard now lets you optimize for Ferrari upgrades and set up value growth through Hulkenberg, Bearman, and Lawson. Only use if your team needs 3+ changes.

chips.name: 3x Boost
chips.reason: No sprint this weekend reduces the total points ceiling. BoxBoxF1Fantasy previously showed 3x boost works best on high-ceiling weekends — consider saving for a sprint weekend or a race where your captain pick is more certain.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Without a sprint, the delta between limitless and a well-constructed normal team is small. Save for a sprint weekend where it can generate a larger advantage.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: COTA Turn 1 chaos is a real risk — Lawson called it 'a lottery.' Having a Final Fix available to swap out a DNF victim could be valuable. Consider holding but being ready to deploy.

watch_items: FP3 pace: Does Ferrari's Friday dominance hold, or do Mercedes/Red Bull close the gap on Saturday? Ferrari have flattered on Fridays before.
Isack Hadjar's comfort with the car — he said it looked 'horrendous' in FP2. If he's still struggling in FP3, downgrade Red Bull constructor in favor of Mercedes + Ferrari.
Turn 1 chaos potential: Multiple drivers have been taken out in T1 at COTA historically. Lawson called it 'a lottery.' Midfield drivers could gain or lose massively on lap 1.
McLaren upgrade dial-in: Norris says big packages take time. Watch if McLaren pace improves through FP3 or if they remain behind Ferrari and Mercedes.
Hulkenberg power unit: FP1 complaints were attributed to setup divergence per Audi team boss McNish, but monitor FP3 for any recurrence.
Track limits enforcement in qualifying — affected Albon in both sessions. Could catch other drivers off guard.
George Russell's race pace on mediums was masked in FP2 — watch FP3 for true Mercedes pace read.
arc: The US GP kicks off a critical end-of-season stretch. Ferrari's upgrades could reshape the constructor hierarchy for the remaining races (Mexico, São Paulo, and beyond). If the upgrades deliver as promised — Leclerc suggested one big package could vault a team from 4th to 1st constructor — Ferrari assets become premium holds through the final triple-header. McLaren's upgrades may take longer to unlock, making them a wait-and-see for Mexico. The value growth plays (Hulkenberg, Bearman, Lawson) are setting up nicely for sustained price appreciation across the final 6 races. Budget managers should be positioning now for maximum team value heading into the season finale stretch, with the Wildcard best used either this weekend or Mexico depending on how Ferrari's upgrades perform in race conditions.
